title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing for OpenAI-compat streaming
author: Lena Rodriguez
description: Fixes a set of related issues in the SSE streaming path that caused partial-JSON payloads and OpenAI-compat clients to see malformed objects or out-of-order token/event sequences. Motivation: production incidents showed that function-calling customers and structured-output consumers occasionally received truncated JSON objects or saw 'data: [partial]' events interleave with delimiter tokens, which broke streaming parsers and caused downstream eval regressions. This PR addresses three root causes: 1) event framing race where token boundaries were emitted before the stream delimiter state machine finished flushing buffered control tokens; 2) partial-JSON boundary handling that split JSON tokens across SSE chunks without emitting an explicit "partial" marker in the expected position; and 3) ordering regressions introduced by the batching refactor that allowed KV-cache flush events to be multiplexed ahead of user-token events in some edge cases. Work performed: - Normalize SSE emission order by introducing an explicit flush window that ensures control delimiters (delimiter, end-of-object) are always emitted before subsequent token events for the same response. - Add a small atomic state transition for partial-JSON sequences so "partial" markers and trailing delimiters are always placed in the canonical order expected by OpenAI-compat parsers. - Ensure the streaming multiplexer respects per-response sequencing when merging KV-cache flush events and model-token deltas. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate chunked sockets, delayed network writes, and interleaved control events (function call start/end, partial JSON boundaries). - Update OpenAI-compat e2e test harness and add a regression test that reproduces the production incident recorded in ENG-1783. Checklist: - [x] Repro case added to test harness - [x] Unit tests for delimiter ordering - [x] Integration tests for chunked sockets - [x] CI green on Linux/macOS - [x] Metric to detect partial-json reorders (telemetry) - [x] Changelog entry for runtime fixes Impact and rollout: The change is backward compatible for standard streaming clients; it tightens ordering guarantees for SSE streams and fixes cases that caused invalid JSON to be emitted. Rolling out to Dedicated/Private follows the normal runtime rollout process; the fix is trivial and low-risk but exercises the streaming hot path so we will monitor the new telemetry metric and error rate over the next 48 hours. Related: ENG-1783, ENG-2102, DOCS-432, and earlier PRs that touched SSE chunking (see history).
commits: test(sse): add chunked-socket regression test for partial-json case
fix(runtime): make streaming multiplexer respect per-response sequencing
ci: add flaky net latency sim in e2e harness
review_comments: Evan Kim: The ordering change looks reasonable, but can you add an assertion to multiplexer tests that checks sequence numbers for correlated events?
Lena Rodriguez: Added the assertion and a comment explaining the flush window semantics; also added an integration test that intentionally delays the control token path to exercise the race.
Priya Desai: CI failed on macOS in the first run — looks like a flaky test that assumes deterministic socket coalescing. Can you make the test tolerant to scheduling?
Lena Rodriguez: Updated the test to use a retry-with-backoff and fixed a timing assumption; reran CI and all checks passed.
Tomás Alvarez: Approved after tests and telemetry metric added. Recommend post-merge watch on 'sse.partial_json_reorders' metric.
Release eng: Please include note for Dedicated rollout (no config changes expected).
release_notes: Fixes several SSE streaming edge cases where partial JSON objects or delimiter tokens could be emitted out of order, causing OpenAI-compat streaming parsers and function-calling clients to fail. This improves streaming stability for structured outputs and function calls.
